newsitem.title: USA: Gunman killed after threat to U.S. hydropower dam.
newsitem.headline: Gunman killed after threat to U.S. hydropower dam.

text.p: An FBI agent shot and killed a gunman outside Bonneville Dam Sunday after the discovery of a tape-recording threatening to blow up a hydropower facility if money was not paid, officials said Monday.

The shooting took place late Sunday after workers at the visitors centre at the dam found a tape recorder with a note saying it should be played, said Diana Brimhall of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, which operates the 57-year-old dam.
On the tape was a demand for $15,000 and a threat to blow up the dam if the demand was not met, FBI officials said.

The visitors centre was closed and staff were evacuating when a man came onto the site with a rifle in one hand and what appeared to be a detonator in the other, asking questions about the money that had been demanded.

FBI, sheriff's deputies and state police had already arrived. As police tried to arrest the gunman, he threatened them with the rifle and was shot by an FBI agent, according to a statement issued by the FBI.
The gunman was identified as Nathaniel Milligan, 18. He was described as a "native American." No further details were given about Mulligan.

No explosive devices were found at the dam, about 40 miles (65 km) east of Portland, Oregon. The visitors centre, on the north side of the Columbia River in Washington state, remained closed while the FBI continued its investigation.
